evidence.claim: Window discovery is provider-neutral, while semantic availability remains dependent on exposed accessibility facts.

A no-activate window with painted pixels and no standard child control is discovered and captured through the production launcher; its absent semantic action target returns ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND without pointer fallback or foreground change.
Real foreground pointer or keyboard effects on custom-drawn content still require named human validation.
Completed pointer input certifies bounded SendInput dispatch and balanced tool ownership, not target-side consumption or physical device origin.
Completed keyboard input certifies bounded SendInput dispatch and balanced tool ownership, not target-side consumption or physical device origin.

Mouse and keyboard NOLEGACY fixtures are discovered and receive WM_INPUT after production launcher dispatch, while both message headers have no device source; the original foreground and cursor are restored.
Real target behavior for synthetic raw-input messages still requires named human validation, especially when an application requires physical device origin.

A tool-owned D3D11 swap chain attempts true DXGI exclusive fullscreen, restores windowed state before release, and the current session reports the official environment-unavailable outcome; actual exclusive discovery and capture remain gaps until the exclusive branch runs.
Exclusive fullscreen visibility, capture, focus, and input remain unverified and cannot be inferred from ordinary windows.

The unchanged production launcher discovers a minimized toolkit window, reports an unavailable hit region, refuses screenshot capture with CAPTURE_TARGET_MINIMIZED, creates no file, and leaves foreground unchanged.
A minimized toolkit window remains classified and does not publish a guessed current-desktop hit region.
Certified capture refuses minimized targets without restoring, showing, or activating them.
Real restore followed by pointer or keyboard interaction remains a named visual and interaction gate.

A toolkit-owned window becomes hidden on one sealed command; production discovery, metadata read, and screenshot routes do not show or activate it, return STALE_SESSION for the old target, create no file, and preserve foreground.
Certified capture refuses hidden targets and never makes a hidden target visible or foreground.
Use-time rediscovery reports stale when an exact public window is no longer discoverable.

A sealed toolkit replacement uses a different current window token; production discovery returns a different opaque identity, metadata and element location reject the old identity with STALE_SESSION, and no title-based rebinding occurs in this distinct-token scenario.

Current identity material cannot distinguish an exactly recycled same-process window token. A persistent asynchronous WinEvent registry can classify history only after event delivery and cannot provide lifetime-bound atomic dispatch, so general no-rebind remains a platform gap.
Zero or ambiguous use-time matches fail closed instead of rebinding an old exact window target.
Location and pointer contracts require Per-Monitor-V2 physical coordinates and use-time relocation after DPI changes.
Production window lifecycle readback matches the current active display topology and post-move window DPI, but this host exposes one 96-DPI monitor so no mixed-DPI transition occurred.
No available fixture run crosses two active monitors with different DPI values; real mixed-DPI interaction remains a named visual gate.
Window geometry uses signed virtual-desktop physical pixels and validates final bounds against the current virtual desktop.
The Windows pointer boundary uses signed half-open virtual-screen bounds without assuming a zero origin.

The production launcher preserves the canonical window target and foreground while moving a tool-owned window across every active monitor; the current host exposes one monitor with no negative origin, so cross-monitor behavior remains unexercised.
Real negative-origin and cross-monitor pointer movement remains a named visual and interaction gate.
